thread:
alex: Heads-up — customer ACME (chat app) flagged p99 latency regressions when we enable default batching. They require <=250ms p99 for short prompts (~<64 tokens). Can we sketch what the Optimize advisor should recommend for a latency-first profile? @priya @mike

priya: Quick clarifying Q — are they on Hosted or Dedicated? that changes our levers (Dedicated = more headroom for batching).

alex: Hosted (paid tier). Traffic is bursty mobile. They want an advisor suggestion in Console + an API flag `latency_first=true`.

mike: Short take: for Hosted + bursty mobile we should bias toward smaller batches and aggressive prefix caching for repeated prompts. Example tradeoffs: batch_size=1 gives best latency but wastes GPU throughput; adaptive batching with very low max_batch_latency (5-10ms) may hit p99 target while preserving some throughput.

sarah: Also add quantization guidance: recommend int8 if model verifier shows <1% quality delta on the customer's eval set. Critical: tie quantization suggestions to eval-triggered alerts so we catch quality regressions quickly.

alex: Can someone draft minimal launch acceptance criteria (health, UX, and safety)?

priya: Draft acceptance criteria (proposal):
- UX: Console shows a "Latency-first" advisor profile and an API flag. Suggestions page explains tradeoffs.
- Runtime: route-level SLOs accepted; advisor can emit recommended config: max_batch_latency, max_batch_size, cache.policy + quantization profile.
- Safeguards: automatic eval-triggered alert when quality metric (customer eval set concordance) drops >5% vs baseline after applying recommendations.
- Observability: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, model cost per 1k requests, and eval-concordance exposed.
- Rollout: gated to 10 pilot customers, 72h observation window, automatic rollback to conservative profile on regressions.

mike: Implementation notes / config sketch:

route.config.slo = { "p99_ms": 250 }
advisor.profile = "latency-first"
batcher.max_latency_ms = 8
batcher.max_batch_size = 8
cache.mode = "prefix-kv"
quant.profile = "int8-if-safe"

Edge: need to ensure batcher respects per-customer burst shaping and token-length heuristics.

sarah: Metrics to track for pilot: p50/p95/p99 latency, cold-start latency, tokens/sec, batching efficiency (avg batch size), model error rate on eval set, and false positive rate of eval-alerts.

alex: Risks called out: customer costs may increase (more GPU ops per token), throughput drop under sustained traffic, noisy eval alerts from small eval sets. Also UX confusion if advisor flips profiles frequently.

priya: Proposed next steps + owners:
- Engineer spike: adaptive batcher caps & per-route SLOs (2w) — owner: mike
- ML: build eval harness + alerting tied to route recommendations (1w) — owner: sarah
- Product/UX: Console mock + API param (1w) — owner: priya
- Ops: pilot runbook + rollback playbook (1w) — owner: alex

mike: I'll pick up the batcher spike. I'll prototype a path that falls back to batch_size=1 for requests under 64 tokens.

sarah: I'll wire the eval harness to send an alert when concordance drops >5% and add a cooldown to prevent flapping.

alex: Great — I'll add INF tickets and slot a 30m prioritization sync tomorrow 10:30am PT to decide Q2 slice. :thumbsup:
